## Description

Muse Spark's DFlash drafter on VANILLA attention keeps its context K/V in a private arena outside the KV cache manager. A prefix-cache hit and a disaggregated context transfer never reach that arena, so those requests draft without their context and the acceptance length (AL) drops. With TRTLLM attention the drafter's K/V lives in the target's KV cache manager, so it is reused on a prefix hit and transferred to the generation worker. With rejection sampling (RS) on top, the natural AL matches the SemiAnalysis golden, which was collected with sampled drafts.

items.body:
Stack: #48831 → **this PR** → #48833

## Motivation

Under compact verify (`SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact`), DeepSeek-V4.1's ratio 1 and 2 compressors run the general torch path, `_low_ratio_compress_torch`. ## Overview

Fixes #50788. Gemma 4 now uses `videos_kwargs.max_soft_tokens` for video frames, as Transformers does. The default stays 70.

items.title: [https://nvbugs/7034340][fix] Free the executor in the rank-local worker teardown
items.author: trtllm-agent
items.summary: Fixes a GPU memory leak in worker teardown by calling the engine cleanup hook through self.engine so gc.collect can free the PyExecutor before empty_cache.
items.body:
## Description

`GenerationExecutorWorker._shutdown_rank_local()` ends with `gc.collect()` and `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` so that a worker process that outlives its LLM, such as a worker of an MPI pool that hosts successive LLM instances, returns the executor's GPU memory before the next LLM is built in it. Since #19646 the method binds the engine's `local_cleanup` hook to a local variable. The bound method keeps the `PyExecutor` reachable until the method returns, so the collection cannot free the executor's reference cycles, and the model they reference stays allocated after `empty_cache()`.

items.title: [Fix] disaggregation: Fail a prefill KV transfer whose decode never completes it
items.author: ydaiming
items.summary: Once a room is past, the sender has no deadline of its own. It waits for the decode to either complete the transfer or abort it (the decode's sends an back to the prefill).
items.body:
## Motivation

Once a room is past `Bootstrapping`, the sender has no deadline of its own. It waits for the decode to either complete the transfer or abort it (the decode's `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_WAITING_TIMEOUT` sends an `ABORT` back to the prefill). A decode that crashes mid-transfer does neither, and a transport error that does not surface as an exception in the transfer worker leaves the room `Transferring`. The request then stays in `disagg_prefill_inflight_queue` until the prefill is restarted, pinning its KV blocks and a metadata-buffer slot.

items.title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Honor and normalize explicit VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT
items.author: yeshihai
items.summary: Worker-side cache spec construction ignores explicit VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT env var and fails to normalize alias layout names to canonical names, causing layout mismatch rejection.
items.body:
## Overview

HiSparse hybrid models build cache specs in the worker before the engine core resolves the KV cache layout, and workers adopt the engine's layout by name. An explicit `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT` can therefore be invisible during worker-side spec setup, and an alias layout name can make the worker reject the canonical layout.

This applies an explicit `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT` at config construction and stores its canonical name. It is a generic config fix with no model-specific behavior.

Links: #59176 (GLM-5.3-Flash + HiSparse layout mismatch). #61243 is the related open PR adding GLM-5.

items.author: shuoerw
items.summary: The SGLang Python backend supports this field, so the same request behaves differently when sent directly to the worker versus through the gateway. Requests intended to use separate cache namespaces can consequently reuse the default namespace.

When sending a `/v1/chat/completions` request through `sgl-model-gateway`, the top-level `cache_salt` field is silently dropped before forwarding to the worker.

items.title: [Fix] kimi-k3: Rebuild derived weights in place on weight updates
items.author: Memory-cq-arch
items.summary: Fixes the CUDA graph address drift issue during RL weight updates for Kimi-K3 and related models. During online weight updates (e.g., RL training), derived tensors (like,,, ) were re-allocated with new memory addresses.
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes the CUDA graph address drift issue during RL weight updates for Kimi-K3 and related models. 

During online weight updates (e.g., RL training), derived tensors (like `w_kc`, `w_vc`, `_bfa_w`, `_front_w`) were re-allocated with new memory addresses. Because these tensors are captured by CUDA graphs, the graphs continued reading stale data from the old addresses, leading to severe accuracy crashes. This PR implements the RFC guideline (in-place updates for graph-visible derived state) to fix this.

## Modifications

1. **`attn_residual.py`**: Extracted the cache product calc

items.author: qinqinwo
items.summary: Fixes pipeline-parallel decoder replay failure when a PP stage begins exactly at the SWA replay cut, causing AssertionError and incorrect write_kv on NVIDIA GPUs.
items.body:
## Overview

On NVIDIA GPUs, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with `--pipeline-parallel-size 2` and decoder SWA bounded replay (the default) fails at startup. The default split of the 40 layers is 20/20, so the second stage starts at layer 20, which is both the last KV source and the replay cut. This PR handles a stage that starts at the cut: the forward skips the then-empty range of non-replay layers, and `write_kv` gets the stage-entry branch that `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer.forward` already has.

This is the NVIDIA counterpart of #64051 (ROCm).

- Fixes the `AssertionError` in `DeepseekV4Model.

items.author: MichaelLapshin

items.body:
## Overview

Currently, MRV2 does not manage the global flag `cudagraph_capturing_enabled`. Therefore:
1. An illegal CUDA graph capture may occur during MRV2 runtime.
2. MRV2 CUDA graph capture raises a error if `cudagraph_capturing_enabled` is false.

## Claims

This PR correctly manages the global flag during MRV2's CUDA graph capturing.

## Validation

This PR unit tests that the global flag is correctly set during and after MRV2's CUDA graph capturing.
```
python -m pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py -v -k test_capture_reenables_cudagraph_capturing
```

items.title: [Bugfix][MoRIIO] Let decode renew READ block leases on prefill
items.author: amirakb89
items.summary: Fixes MoRIIO READ mode where decode reads freed/reused KV blocks after prefill's defer_timeout expires, by implementing lease renewal.
items.body:
## Overview

In MoRIIO READ mode, prefill frees a request's KV blocks `defer_timeout` (60 s) after the request finishes, even if decode has not read them yet. A request that waits longer than that in decode's queue then reads blocks prefill has already reused, and its output is silently wrong. This PR turns that fixed timeout into a lease that decode renews until it reads the request, following NIXL's KV lease design ([`nixl_kv_cache_lease.md`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/design/nixl_kv_cache_lease.md)).

This is Gap 2 of [ROCm/mori#759](https://github.com/ROCm/mori/iss

items.author: wirybeaver
items.summary: KDA's safe-gate diagonal kernels use different normalization anchors: the fused path uses the first token of each 16-token subchunk, while the unfused path uses its midpoint. The anchor cancels algebraically, but changes finite-precision rounding.

KDA's safe-gate diagonal kernels use different normalization anchors: the fused path uses the first token of each 16-token subchunk, while the unfused path uses its midpoint. ## Motivation

`fused_recurrent_kda` (the KDA decode path) carried commented-out `ssm_state_indices` plumbing, so every caller had to gather each request's fp32 `[HV, V, K]` state out of the pool into a packed buffer, run the kernel, and scatter the result back. For a KDA layer with 24 heads of 128 that is two full-state copies per layer per decode step on top of the kernel's own read and write. The packed-decode kernels in the same file already address the pool by slot; this gives the generic recurrent kernel the same ability.

## Overview

On ROCm, `MoERunner` now applies the gate it holds (the router GEMM) before the shared experts fork onto the aux stream, instead of right after the fork. items.title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] dsv41: Gather 8 local Engram rows per program on SM103 and SM107
items.author: dmtri35
items.summary: 's local kernel runs one Triton program per looked-up row. Each program is a chain of dependent loads (id, then payload and scales) ending in a 512-byte store. [Discussion: Could we just use 16?]
items.body:
## Motivation

`engram_gather`'s local kernel (`_engram_gather_kernel`) runs one Triton program per looked-up row. Each program is a chain of dependent loads (id, then payload and scales) ending in a 512-byte store. In a DeepSeek-V4.1 DP prefill a forward makes two such calls of `ranks x tokens x 24` rows: 3.1M programs at 32K tokens per rank on 4 ranks. Per-program latency, not bandwidth, bounds the kernel. On 4x VR200 at 32K tokens per rank each call took 1.67 ms, about 1.5% of the forward.

The peer-read kernel (`_engram_gather_peer_kernel`, #46180) already runs 8 rows per program. This PR
discussion: Could we just use 16? Seems 0.1µs slow in low bs is ok to ignore.

items.author: xsxszab
items.summary: Fixes multimodal prefix-LM models losing bidirectional attention over image tokens on non-first PP stages due to encoder cache only being built on the first rank.
items.body:
## Overview

With Model Runner V2 and pipeline parallelism, multimodal prefix-LM models (Gemma3, PaliGemma, and others with `is_mm_prefix_lm`) lose bidirectional attention over image tokens on every PP stage after the first. `DefaultModelState.prepare_attn` reads the image ranges from the encoder cache, but the model runner creates the encoder cache only on the first PP rank. Later stages build causal-only attention metadata, and the output is silently wrong.

## Summary

In `load_moe_expert_weights`, a sliced/transposed fused MoE expert weight view is passed to `weight_loader()` and copied to GPU while still non-contiguous. Add support for feeding the previous token’s final hidden state into the current token’s input, following the shared idea in [Full-bandwidth Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08888v2) and [Recycler](https://seed.bytedance.com/en/public_papers/recycler-cost-free-latent-reasoning-via-hidden-state-recycling).

items.author: SuperGoodGame
items.summary: An existing MoE checkpoint can be served with a calibrated subset of routed experts by passing. The model allocates weights only for retained physical slots, while its router keeps the original logical expert IDs.
items.body:
An existing MoE checkpoint can be served with a calibrated subset of routed experts by passing `--moe-expert-profile`. The model allocates weights only for retained physical slots, while its router keeps the original logical expert IDs. This lets deployments evaluate and use different expert profiles without rewriting a checkpoint for each profile.

For example, given a model with eight routed experts per layer, this profile stores four experts per layer and preserves the specified slot order:

```json
{"num_experts": 8, "keep": [[7, 1, 5, 3], [6, 2, 4, 0]]}
```

## Description

### Problem

- Slurm's GCP NCCL overrides can be lost when a multi-node launcher starts another Bash and the image re-enables its profiler. Moving settings into a packaged helper also leaves reused build artifacts on old settings.

## Overview

The DeepSeek-V4.1 K-cache gather kernels compute each output row offset in int32. Once a prefill gather chunk passes 2^31 elements, rows are written about 4 GiB outside the workspace. On MI355X, this crashes DeepSeek-V4.1 startup with DSpark adaptive verification at TP8.

No expected NVIDIA impact: CUDA uses the CuteDSL gather for fp8/MXFP8 (NVFP4 is already int64 since #63018), so these kernels run there only as a fallback, where offsets below 2^31 are unchanged.

items.author: Heisenberg-Yin

items.body:
## Motivation

DSA-style sparse attention (GLM-5.x, DeepSeek-V4.1) selects the top-k keys for each prefill row from indexer scores over all visible keys. In the dense baseline evaluated here, DeepGEMM `mqa_logits` materializes the full `[rows, keys]` logits, then a separate top-k reads them back. At long context, both the logits traffic and selection work grow with `rows x keys`. The logits-memory budget also forces large prefills into smaller scoring calls.

This PR replaces the kernel behind `fused_mqa_topk` with the sampled-threshold path of [LiteTopK](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11976),

## Motivation

The image mixes hand-pinned compute-runtime/IGC/gmmlib debs with the rolling kobuk PPA, and they have drifted apart: the pinned gmmlib is too old for the PPA's iHD driver, so apt silently drops it and the image has no VA-API video decode (needed by #48074). Intel's versioned intel-omix channel ships one tested, consistent set instead, as vLLM uses.

The channel version is a build arg; override with `--build-arg INTEL_OMIX_VERSION=<version>`.

|---|---|---|
| Compute runtime | 26.27.39122.11 | 26.31.39395.16 |

Out-of-tree backends cannot use the existing tensor weight-update path without changing core serialization code: `monkey_patch_torch_reductions()` only handles the built-in CUDA/NPU paths, and `SafeUnpickler` rejects backend-owned rebuild functions. Standalone training senders that only use SGLang's serialization utilities do not automatically call `load_plugins()`. ## Motivation

On HIP, DeepSeek-V4's breakable prefill graphs cannot keep the decoder SWA tail. `DecoderReplayTail`, which #45107 added to run the layers after the last KV-source layer on each request's last 128 rows inside prefill-graph steps, is created only on CUDA, and its KV store asserts that the query RoPE is not fused into the store, which it is on HIP. #48148 makes these graphs capture on HIP by dropping the tail, so those layers (20-39 for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) run every prompt row. items.title: [Perf][MiniMax-M3] Don't sync when building sparse-attention prefill metadata
items.author: MrGeva
items.summary: zeroes the first prefill entry with on CUDA. Assigning a Python scalar to an element of a CUDA tensor is a pageable host-to-device copy, so the host waits for all queued GPU work. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

`MiniMaxM3SparseMetadataBuilder.build` zeroes the first prefill `cu_seqlens_k` entry with `prefill_cu_seqlens_k[0] = 0` on CUDA. Assigning a Python scalar to an element of a CUDA tensor is a pageable host-to-device copy, so the host waits for all queued GPU work. The metadata is built while the previous step is still running on the GPU, so every step that contains a prefill stalls the host until the GPU drains. items.author: frankie-ys
items.summary: On decode steps where no block was appended (the common case between block-boundary crossings), the flush re-copies an unchanged buffer. On platforms with mapped pinned host memory each is a cheap CPU-side memcpy, but on the fallback path — no mapped pinned me…
items.body:
## Summary / motivation

`BlockTables.apply_staged_writes()` ends with an unconditional
`num_blocks.copy_to_uva()` on every step, but `num_blocks.np` is written only
in `append_block_ids`. On decode steps where no block was appended (the
common case between block-boundary crossings), the flush re-copies an
unchanged buffer.

On platforms with mapped pinned host memory each `copy_to_uva` is a cheap
CPU-side memcpy, but on the fallback path — no mapped pinned memory, which is
the common case on non-CUDA platforms such as Ascend — every flush issues a
real H2D copy with per-call launch overhead.

## Overview

`PoolingBaseServing` hands each request's render and postprocessing to the renderer thread pool one call at a time (`make_async`). For short pooling requests, submitting the job costs the event loop about as much as the work itself. This PR adds `make_async_batched`, which hands the calls made in one event-loop iteration to at most one executor job per worker, and uses it for `render_async` and `_postprocessing_async`. The jobs take the calls from a shared queue as they become free, so calls spread over the workers as they do with one job per call, and each result is handed back

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Resample synthetic rejections from the target distribution
items.author: cquil11
items.summary: Synthetic acceptance rejects drafts with a seeded coin flip, not a p/q test, but the rejected slot is still resampled from max(p - q, 0). That residual is only the right conditional after a real rejection.
items.body:
Synthetic acceptance rejects drafts with a seeded coin flip, not a p/q test, but the rejected slot is still resampled from max(p - q, 0). That residual is only the right conditional after a real rejection. Under synthetic acceptance it drops the mass the draft agrees with and over-samples tokens the draft under-weights, such as channel and tool delimiters, which strict tool parsers then turn into empty responses.

This resamples the rejected slot from the target distribution when synthetic acceptance is enabled. Acceptance timing is unchanged, and non-synthetic paths are untouched.

Addresses
discussion: Closing: this had no measurable effect on the empty-response rate in end-to-end testing. The parser-side fix is in #65872.

## What does this PR do?

next step only when every draft is accepted. Otherwise it keeps its row, its

With speculative decoding (MTP), an eager decode-only step pads its request

### What does this PR do?

Adds a **MaxText (JAX) actor engine** to the v1 `separate_async` trainer, so Qwen3-30B-A3B can be trained with GRPO on AMD MI300X (ROCm) while vLLM serves rollouts from a separate node. The engine plugs in as `model_engine=maxtext`. It does not touch the FSDP or Megatron paths.

Scope and limits:
- There is no ref model/KL and no critic.
- The engine supports Qwen3-MoE only. The HF to MaxText weight mapping tables are specific to that architecture.
- It targets the `separate_async` trainer with `hybrid_engine=false`.

items.title: [TRTLLM-16624][fix] Do not specialize spec-decode Triton kernels on batch-dependent arguments
items.author: zhaoyuanh-nvidia
items.summary: Triton specializes integer arguments on and and pointer arguments on 16-byte alignment, and compiles a new kernel variant whenever one of those keys changes. Several speculative-decoding step kernels take arguments whose keys follow the batch composition, so t…
items.body:
## Description

Triton specializes integer arguments on `== 1` and `% 16 == 0` and pointer arguments on 16-byte alignment, and compiles a new kernel variant whenever one of those keys changes. Several speculative-decoding step kernels take arguments whose keys follow the batch composition, so they compile new variants mid-serving, after warmup:

- request counts
- first-row offsets
- pair-layout offsets derived from the row count
- views sliced at the number of context requests

Each compile blocks every rank of the replica while it runs. On GB300 with Kimi K3 and DSpark (K=5), this showed up

items.title: [#21643][fix] Flush Poolside stream text at completion
items.author: 0z5a
items.summary: When a stream ends with a partial marker, Poolside v1 keeps the surrounding text in its buffer and inherits the no-op, so the client never receives it. A stream ending inside an incomplete call has the same problem.
items.body:
## Description

When a stream ends with a partial `<tool_call>` marker, Poolside v1 keeps the surrounding text in its buffer and inherits the no-op `finish()`, so the client never receives it. A stream ending inside an incomplete call has the same problem.

Release the remaining buffer once at completion. This matches the existing whole-response parser's treatment of incomplete blocks and preserves text after completed calls.

Fixes #21643.

items.title: Add an optional TensorAtomic placement for MCore MFSDP v2 dense parameters
items.author: Autumn1998
items.summary: Muon needs each weight matrix whole on one rank to run Newton-Schulz. MFSDP v2 shards the matrices, so today the optimizer step gathers each matrix's pieces to an owner rank and scatters the update back.
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Muon needs each weight matrix whole on one rank to run Newton-Schulz. MFSDP v2 shards the matrices, so today the optimizer step gathers each matrix's pieces to an owner rank and scatters the update back. This PR adds an optional alternative: with `MFSDP_TENSOR_ATOMIC=1`, every dense parameter stays whole on one owner rank (the `TensorAtomic` placement), so the Muon step needs no gather or scatter. Owners are chosen greedily to balance the Newton-Schulz cost. The plan depends only on parameter shapes, so every rank computes the same one. Experts keep their own mesh.

items.title: [ray] fix: prevent master port races during worker startup
items.author: SeptPonts
items.summary: Prevent during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore. Previously, probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Prevent `EADDRINUSE` during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore.

Previously, `RayWorkerGroup` probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers. Another process could claim that port before rank zero initialized its process group.

Rank zero now binds and retains the actual TCPStore before invoking the user worker constructor. It publishes the bound endpoint before that constructor can block waiting for peers, allowing the driver to start the remaining ranks.

items.title: Fix math_dapo Minerva extraction for markdown-decorated answers
items.author: siddhant-rajhans
items.summary: The existing regex captures the markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0. Fixes #8449 ## Root cause The Minerva answer pattern matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line.
items.body:
## Bug

Models commonly wrap the Minerva `Answer:` label in markdown bold/italic (`**Answer:** 42`, `Answer: **42**`, `**Answer:**\n\n42`). The existing regex captures the `*` markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0.

Fixes #8449

## Root cause

The Minerva answer pattern `(?i)Answer\s*:\s*([^\n]+)` matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line. When models decorate with markdown:

| Input | Extracted | After normalize | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| `**Answer:** 42` | `** 42` | `**42` | -1.0 |
| `Answer: **42**` | `**42**` | `**42**` |

items.body:
## Problem

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

With valid finite log-probabilities near -0.1, I reproduced a value of -1.4901161e-8 where an 80-digit reference gives 4.9986626e-11. The helper feeds the reported KL term and configured KL loss/reward paths; the Search-R1 example selects `low_var_kl` with a nonzero KL-loss coefficient.

### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8433.

`SFTTrainer` built its train/val `StatefulDataLoader`s without a `generator`, so every iterator construction drew a `base_seed` from the global CPU RNG. On resume that draw happens right after the checkpoint manager restores `torch.get_rng_state()`, so the resumed run continued from a different global CPU RNG state than an uninterrupted run. This PR gives each dataloader its own seeded `torch.Generator`, so building iterators no longer touches the global CPU RNG and the restored state is the one training actually continues with.

With `--sglang-speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and a colocated rollout engine, the first weight sync silently overwrites the DFLASH draft with target weights. After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off.

items.title: fix(sglang): validate deployment config before launch
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

## Background

`exec_and_wait` launches commands in detached sessions so they can survive transport retries, but its timeout and cancellation paths previously stopped waiting without stopping the detached command.

## Problem

A timed-out or cancelled sandbox command could keep running and mutate the sandbox after the caller had already moved on. There was also a race between launch acknowledgement and publishing the detached process group PID.

## Solution

- Record the detached session leader PID before executing the launcher.

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Rank 0 was especially vulnerable because it was added to only after its rendezvous lookup succeeded. The non-empty handler list also prevented a clean retry.
items.body:
## Background

`RayTrainGroup.create()` allocates training actors sequentially, discovers the rank-0 rendezvous address, initializes every actor, and optionally attaches the rollout manager.

## Problem

A failure at any of those stages left already-created actors alive. Rank 0 was especially vulnerable because it was added to `_actor_handlers` only after its rendezvous lookup succeeded. The non-empty handler list also prevented a clean retry.

## Solution

- Register each actor immediately after creation, before rank-0 rendezvous lookup.
- Treat allocation, actor initialization, and rollout-m

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ

## Problem

The remote reward model caches one process-global `aiohttp.ClientSession`. Standard rollout/eval work uses the shared background event loop, while fully-async rollout owns a separate thread and loop. Reusing the same session across those live loops can fail with loop-affinity errors, and the cached session had no owner-driven shutdown path.

## Change

- Store one shared remote-RM session per running event loop behind a short thread-safe registry lock.
- Reuse sessions within a loop while keeping concurrently live loops isolated.

items.title: fix(agent): linearize session shutdown with request admission
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Shutdown can snapshot an empty inflight set immediately before a request registers itself, allowing to return before that admitted turn is recorded. Requests admitted first are drained by shutdown.
items.body:
## Problem

Adapter request admission and `shutdown_session()` update `closed` and `inflight` from different event-loop threads without synchronization. Shutdown can snapshot an empty inflight set immediately before a request registers itself, allowing `finish_session()` to return before that admitted turn is recorded.

## Change

- Add a per-adapter lock around the session admission boundary.
- Linearize the closed check, turn-cap update, session lookup, and inflight registration with shutdown's closed mark and inflight snapshot.

## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

items.body:
## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

## Summary

`--kl-coef` is reward-KL shaping. GRPO-style estimators (`grpo`, `gspo`, `cispo`) do not apply KL to rewards, so a non-zero `--kl-coef` is a silent no-op today.

items.body:
Fixes #1369.

`distributed_masked_whiten(..., shift_mean=False)` used to center, scale, then add the mean back:

```
whitened_values = (values - global_mean) * rsqrt(var)
if not shift_mean:

```

That is not a scale-only path. This change makes `shift_mean` do what it says:

- `shift_mean=True` (default): `(values - global_mean) * rsqrt(global_var + epsilon)` — zero-mean, unit-variance
- `shift_mean=False`: `values * rsqrt(global_var + epsilon)` — scale only; do not subtract the mean, and do not add it back

items.title: fix: cancel pending rollout tasks after a failure
items.author: yuyz-cyber
items.summary: When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task except…
items.body:
## Problem

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task exceptions in the event loop.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

items.title: require --ref-load when KL is enabled instead of crashing with a TypeError
items.author: rootkiller6788
items.summary: Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slimevalidateargs with, because it stat'd args.refload before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.
items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

items.title: fix: preserve equals in extra environment values
items.author: imshunsuke
items.summary: For example: was parsed as: This corrupts padded or otherwise -containing environment values. JSON input handling and the existing fallback tokenization remain unchanged.
items.body:
## Summary

- Preserve `=` characters after the first separator in the space-separated `extra_env_vars` fallback parser.
- Add regression coverage to the always-on CPU test matrix.

## Problem

`_parse_extra_env_vars` split each assignment on every `=` and then kept only the second component. For example:

`TOKEN=abc== END=ok`

was parsed as:

`{"TOKEN": "abc", "END": "ok"}`

This corrupts padded or otherwise `=`-containing environment values.

## Change

Use `split("=", 1)` so only the key/value separator is consumed. JSON input handling and the existing fallback tokenization remain unchanged

## Problem

`--rollout-temperature 0` is greedy decoding. That is not a usable on-policy RL policy: the sampling distribution is a delta, while log-probs (and PPO ratios) still come from a softmax. Greedy RL should be rejected at config parse, not assumed away in loss code.

`--eval-temperature 0` is unchanged; greedy eval remains valid.

## Change

`slime_validate_args` raises if `rollout_temperature <= 0`.

## Test plan

items.body:
## Summary

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

## Problem

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when
used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.

- Reuse the existing `_wrap_ipv6` helpe

items.title: fix rollout GPU placement validation keyword
items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: Every non-debug rollout startup on current therefore raised before engines were launched.
items.body:
## Summary

- align `ServerGroup.start_engines()` with the renamed `num_gpus_per_engine_on_node` validation keyword
- keep the local variable name consistent with the validator and GPU-index calculation

## Root cause

The rollout GPU-placement validator renamed its keyword to `num_gpus_per_engine_on_node`, but the call site still passed `num_gpu_per_engine`. Every non-debug rollout startup on current `main` therefore raised `TypeError` before engines were launched.

- `python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_rollout_validation.py` (`3 passed`)

## Summary
https://github.com/vllm-project/vime/issues/206
This PR adds end-to-end LoRA support for Megatron actor training with colocated vLLM rollout. When `--lora-rank > 0`, the training actor applies LoRA adapters via Megatron-Bridge, exports PEFT-format adapters after each weight update, and hot-loads them into vLLM through the runtime LoRA API. Rollout requests then use the adapter name instead of the base model path.

This enables parameter-efficient RL fine-tuning without full-weight sync between trainer and inference engines on every step.

This PR is the first step toward the NCCL m2n rollout weight sync proposal in #52.

It adds an opt-in non-colocated weight sync backend:

```text

```

The existing gather-broadcast path remains the default. Colocated rollout engines continue using the existing CUDA IPC path.

- Add `UpdateWeightFromNcclm2n` as an optional non-colocated updater.

items.title: refactor(vllm): use native IPC engine for colocated weight sync
items.author: miracle0517
items.summary: Replace VIME's custom colocated IPC weight-sync implementation with the native weight transfer engines provided by vLLM and vLLM-Ascend. This removes the manual IPC handle gathering, serialization, and worker-side chunk loading path while aligning colocated we…
items.body:
## Summary

Replace VIME's custom colocated IPC weight-sync implementation with the native weight transfer engines provided by vLLM and vLLM-Ascend.

This removes the manual IPC handle gathering, serialization, and worker-side chunk loading path while aligning colocated weight updates with vLLM's native `/update_weights` lifecycle.

## What changed

- Use  `NPUIPCWeightTransferEngine` on Ascend to send colocated weights.
- Route native `update_info` payloads through `VLLMEngine.update_weights` and vLLM's `/update_weights` endpoint.
- Initialize the native weight transfer engine once

items.title: [Bugfix][Training] Avoid entropy grad graph when entropy_coef is zero
items.author: Henry-Jessie
items.summary: This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss. Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary.
items.body:
## Summary

This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss.

Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary. When `entropy_coef == 0`, VIME still computes entropy metrics, but the entropy tensor is only used for reporting and has no gradient contribution. The current implementation always builds the entropy autograd graph and clones the full logits tensor before entropy computation, which increases peak memory without changing the loss.
